scope: Publication-list search and selected mathematical source review, not a full proof audit or an exhaustive classification. Public PDFs and extracted text are not redistributed.
identity_notes: The user confirmed Chung-Jun Tsai and Jonathan J. Zhu, and added Mao-Pei Tsui, Mu-Tao Wang and Wei-Bo Su.
Dominic Joyce and Tang-Kai Lee are the other requested authors. Yng-Ing Lee and Ping-Hung Lee are distinct coauthors; Jingze Zhu is distinct from Jonathan Zhu.

sources.checked: Section 2.2, equations for S and its metric; Proposition 2.2. Unit convention checked against the normalized Möbius map.
Theorem 1.2; Section 2.1, quotient (2.2), metric and shrinker identity; Section 7.2 and Remarks 7.3–7.6, including exact entropy. No genericity theorem inferred.
Theorems A–F, Corollaries H–I, Sections 3–6. Periodic compact case E(a)(ii); plane-neck cases C–D; translator formula (18), with direct integral rewrite; constant-radius rotating subcase of G/H.
Theorems 1.1–1.2, Remark 1.3, Examples 3.9 and 3.15; n ≥ 3, exactness, embeddedness and asymptotic rates retained.
Definition 2.1; Theorem 5.6; Theorem 6.2 and Propositions 6.3/6.5. Concrete nonquadratic seed is an independent substitution into Proposition 6.5.
Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 5.1, Section 5 proof; exact omega-limit set, smooth reparametrized convergence and antipodally invariant nonround metrics.
Main Theorem (p. 4), Theorem 9.1, Proposition 9.5 and Corollary 9.6. m ≥ 3, flat complex torus, one transverse type-one intersection, neck scale and curvature rate.
Sections 2–3 for ambient metric and quotient PDE; Theorem 6.2 and its proof for precise initial slope/concavity hypotheses, N ≥ 3, vanishing H and log curvature / sqrt(t) bounds.

Propositions 2.1–2.2 and Theorem 1.1; unit weights ±1, positive weight sum, explicit mapping-torus quotient retained. Topology and orientability audited directly, including the disconnected-fiber exception to Proposition 2.2 shorthand.
Main Theorem, Corollary 1.1, Sections 2–4 and final perturbation argument; m ≥ 3, admissible angles, T-finite grim-cylinder arrangement, gluing scale distinct from time.
Theorem 5.6, equation (31), Proposition 5.9 and Remark 5.10 for the SO(m−1) stationary family; Sections 5.2–5.4 for overlap and singular-group cautions.
Theorem 1.1, Remark 1 and Section 2.2; restricted SO(n) case, permitted n and K, topology from profile and spherical orbits, multiplicity-one tangent flow, finer Lawlor blow-up limit.
Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.5; entropy means supremum over all flow times. Classification cross-linked to the existing embedded graphical grim-chain family.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-mobius-shrinker
entries.illustration: A finite patch of the exact embedded Möbius quotient in C². Rotation changes the projection; projected crossings do not imply self-intersection.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-jlt-compact-shrinkers
entries.illustration: The ODE and rational phase-closing conditions produce a compact immersion with domain Sⁿ⁻¹ × S¹. No numerical closed orbit or embeddedness is claimed by this picture.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-jlt-translators
entries.illustration: The n = 2, a₁ = α = 1 exact integral parametrization is evaluated numerically and projected from R⁴. The displayed patch is truncated; the full embedded surface has one end.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-jlt-rotating-translators
entries.illustration: The n = 2 map (x eⁱˢ, x²/2 − is) on a finite parameter window. Its last imaginary coordinate separates turns. Use 4D rotation to change the projection.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-jlt-expanders
entries.illustration: The exact integral parametrization in C² with a₁ = a₂ = 1 and α = 1/2, evaluated numerically. Both planar ends are truncated. This is a projection, not an R³ expander.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-ttw-expanders
entries.illustration: The gradient cone of the nonquadratic potential specified in the text, projected from C². It is initial data at t = 0; the positive-time expander is constructed by PDE and is not rendered here.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-lawlor-necks
entries.illustration: A truncated exact Lawlor annulus in C² with a₁ = a₂ = 1. It is stationary under MCF. Projected crossings do not change its embeddedness in R⁴.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-aryan-lee
entries.illustration: The spiral represents a slow parameter approaching a circle of critical points, each indexing a different limiting geodesic. This is not a simulation on a round sphere.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-su-tsai-wood
entries.illustration: Two compact special Lagrangian tori joined by a positive neck, drawn schematically. The dimension is m ≥ 3 in a flat complex torus. Pinching occurs only in the infinite-time limit.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-lee-tsai
entries.illustration: Four collinear centers illustrate a sphere tending to a chain of three special Lagrangian spheres. The positive curves are schematic quotient graphs, not numerical weighted-flow solutions.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-lw-quadric-shrinkers
entries.illustration: The s = 0 real slice x₁² + x₂² − x₃² = 2 in C³. It is only a two-dimensional slice of a three-manifold in R⁶; the circle action supplies the missing dimension.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-lw-quadric-expanders
entries.illustration: The s = 0 real slice x₁² + x₂² − x₃² = −2 in C³. Its two sheets join through the circle quotient in the connected three-dimensional expander.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-su-glued-translators
entries.illustration: Two intersecting grim cylinders in Cᵐ, m ≥ 3, are replaced by a small Lawlor neck and perturbed to a translator. This is a schematic, not an exact surface or a numerical PDE solution.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-su-wood-stationary
entries.illustration: The exact planar Lawlor profile ℓ(s) = (cos(2s))^(−1/2)eⁱˢ used twice when m = 3. This is an auxiliary curve, not the full stationary three-manifold in C³.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-stolarski-su
entries.illustration: Schematic neck profiles at decreasing scales comparable to (T − t)^(K/2). The full flow lies in Cⁿ, n ≥ 3, and is constructed by PDE; these are not computed time slices.

exclusions: JLT nonperiodic bounded/quasiperiodic immersions and mixed-sign periodic quadrics are not catalogued in this selected addition; no completeness/properness or entropy is guessed for them.
The JLT constant-radius compact shrinkers overlap familiar examples and are excluded from the new compact-periodic entry.
Joyce’s conjectural surgery program is recorded as context, not a proved example or a classification.
Lee–Zhao and Chen–Lee–Sun–Zhao compact realizations of prescribed hypersurface singularities are already discussed in the catalogue source audit; their shrinker models are not duplicated.
Jonathan Zhu’s rigidity, entropy, uniqueness and free-boundary regularity papers are reviewed as context; existing spheres, cylinders and Clifford products are not duplicated.
No weak Brakke continuation through the Möbius cone is claimed; quotient multiplicities require a separate audit.
Other Lee–Wang integer weights are not conflated with the reviewed embedded unit-weight n ≥ 3 cases; no weak-flow multiplicity is inferred for a different quotient.

Su–Wood line/expander translators duplicate the symmetric JLT subfamily. Nonconstant shrinker/line translators and general-group immersed or singular cases are described in the source review but are outside this selected addition.

Tsai–Wang special-holonomy stability supplies stationary zero sections and nearby immortal flows; these are recorded as contextual candidates, with exact ambient metrics and smallness hypotheses, rather than merged with Euclidean examples.
